body.statement:
Under the formal specialization of the displayed constructions to \(m=1\), one has \(B=A\) and \(Q=D\). Consequently, \(\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) is empty when \((B,Q)\) violates any fine-grid compatibility constraint and otherwise equals the singleton \(\{(B,Q)\}\). Accordingly, on an admissible exact input the certificate returns incompatibility in the first case, while in the second case it returns the unique transfer
\[
h_{uv}(z)=\frac{B_{vu}z}{1-B_{vv}z},
\]
which is the standard unaliased direct process transfer.
body.justification: This verifies that the new machinery collapses to the familiar fine-grid formula when aliasing is removed.
body.gap: The reduction is not a novelty claim; it is the required fidelity check against standard process-graph transfer analysis.
body.consumer: Implementers can test the certificate against an unaliased benchmark before using it on subsampled data.
body.proof_tex:
Extend the constructions in \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate}\) to the formal case \(m=1\). By the defining equations of the compatible fiber,
\[
B=A^1=A
\]
and, using \(A^0=I_d\),
\[
Q=\sum_{r=0}^{0}A^rD(A^r)^{\top}=A^0D(A^0)^{\top}=D.
\]
Hence every \((A,D)\in\mathcal S(B,Q;G)\) must equal \((B,Q)\), so the fiber has at most one element. Conversely, substituting \((A,D)=(B,Q)\) into \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\mbox{-}fiber}\) shows that this pair belongs to the fiber exactly when \(B_{ij}=0\) for \(i<j\), \(B_{ij}=0\) for every \(i>j\) with \(j\to i\notin G\), \(\max_i|B_{ii}|<1\), \(Q_{ij}=0\) for \(i\ne j\), and \(Q\succ0\). Thus the fiber is empty if any of these constraints fails and is \(\{(B,Q)\}\) otherwise.

It remains to verify the algorithmic output rather than infer it merely from the cardinality assertion. For \(m=1\), each diagonal root equation used by \(\operatorname{Cert}_{uv,1,G}\) is
\[
a_{ii}=B_{ii},
\]
and therefore has exactly one real branch. Moreover, directly from the declared divided-difference polynomial,
\[
C_1(x,y)=\sum_{r=0}^{0}x^r y^{0-r}=1.
\]
A length-one nondecreasing walk cannot contain two strict increases, so the declared indirect-path remainder satisfies \(R_{vu,1}=0\). The triangular recursion therefore gives, coordinate by coordinate,
\[
B_{vu}=A_{vu}C_1(A_{vv},A_{uu})+R_{vu,1}=A_{vu}.
\]
Thus no divided-difference coordinate is singular and the certificate has only the candidate \(A=B\); the coarse covariance equation then gives only \(D=Q\). The exact compatibility filtering in \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate}\) rejects this candidate and returns incompatibility precisely when the fiber is empty, and otherwise accepts it. In the latter case the two-copy transfer-inequality system is infeasible because both copies equal \((B,Q)\), so the common-transfer branch of the certificate returns
\[
h_{uv}(z)=\frac{A_{vu}z}{1-A_{vv}z}=\frac{B_{vu}z}{1-B_{vv}z}.
\]
Finally, compatibility gives \(|B_{vv}|<1\); since \(|z|=1\), one has \(|B_{vv}z|<1\), whence \(1-B_{vv}z\ne0\). The displayed rational transfer is therefore well defined on \(\mathbb T\), completing the claimed unaliased reduction.
